[2026-07-29 | AAPL | Underweight | -8.0% | -13.6% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Trim AAPL into strength: sell roughly one-third of the existing position into the $338–$345 area (today's $344.57 high caps the workable zone), initiate no new longs at $338.19, and do not short — the trend stack is fully intact and squeeze risk above $346.14 is real. Cap any residual at ~0.5x a normal AAPL allocation (0.3–0.4x if concentrated or a double-digit gap is intolerable), since ATR is $8.02 (2.37%) and the name already gapped −6.1% in one session. Manage on closes: above $346.14 on >60M shares halts further selling and forces reassessment (not an add-back trigger); below $319–$322.40 triggers another cut; below the 50-SMA at $308.59 clears the remaining tactical exposure. Horizon 1–3 months, fully re-underwritten at the 2026-07-30 print.

**Investment Thesis**: All three seats converge on reducing exposure (aggressive 0.5x with a re-entry mandate, conservative two-thirds sell, neutral one-third to one-half), so direction is settled and only size is contested; the neutral construction wins.

The decisive evidence is arithmetic the trader and neutral got right: $338.19 against the fundamentals report's own unverified ~$8.40 FY2026E midpoint EPS ($8.00–$8.80) is 38x–42x, and the $389 measured move the technical report derives requires 46x on that midpoint — a second re-rating, not earnings delivery, bought at a $5T market cap into a dated binary event. The bull case is real but already capitalized: H1 revenue +16.1%, Q2 gross margin 49.27%, FCF +63.5%, 1.15x cash conversion, ~$62B net cash, and a stacked rising structure (338.19 > 10-EMA 330.84 > 50-SMA 308.59 > 200-SMA 277.21, MACD histogram +1.17, no overhead supply above 344.57). But none of that is a floor — June 25 printed −6.1% on 107.0M shares and June 26 capitulated on 261.8M versus only 61–63M on the July breakout days, so the year's deepest liquidity sits on the sell side.

Durability is where the bull loses. Only two quarters are visible, FY2025 is unavailable in the cache, OpEx is outgrowing revenue, and the margin story depends on gross margin holding near record levels — the report's own linchpin, tested by the print. The Q2 buyback collapsed to $12.3B (−53% sequential and YoY), mechanically halving the share-count tailwind that manufactured EPS growth above net income growth. The $12.8B intangible build against ~$14.0B of noncurrent liabilities with no matching cash outflow is material and unexplained at this multiple, and the 17.46% ETR vs 15.00% prior (~$0.14/share H1 drag) may not be in consensus.

I reject both extremes. The aggressive analyst's "certain gain" plus pre-committed redeploy-at-more-size is relabeled market timing: if the print is good he buys back higher or not at all, and the $338.19 sale is the only certainty. The conservative's two-thirds default is too blunt against an intact rising stack, a de-risking balance sheet (~$61.9B net cash) and zero evidence of franchise deterioration — that is a portfolio-context call, not a blanket rule. A Sell/full exit and any naked short are unsupported: price is above every major average, %B ~0.83 leaves room to $346.14, and squeeze risk is real.

Prior lessons govern execution, not direction. The 2026-06-30, 07-01, 07-13, 07-20, 07-21 and 07-22 AAPL Underweights each cost +3.2% to +6.2% of five-day alpha by trimming an intact uptrend on momentum decay or nearby-level logic; the fix was to require a real trigger and shrink size rather than sell. This trim is different in kind — sized against a known dated event and a 38–42x multiple — but the lesson is why it stays at the light end, keeps a meaningful residual, refuses an automated add-back above $346.14, and does not chase a volume breakout. The 2026-07-22 AMZN lesson (weight divergence over the "trend intact, trim light" prior) is why this is not a Hold.

What would change it: a daily close above $346.14 on >60M shares halts the trim; post-print evidence of gross margin ≥48%, ETR ≤~17.5% reflected in consensus, Q3 buybacks above $20B and a benign explanation of the $12.8B intangible / ~$14B liability justifies a staged rebuild of part of the trimmed amount, deliberately not full size; a reset toward the ~$250–$270 valuation grid (≈30x on ~$8.40) materially improves the entry. Downgrades: a close below $319–$322.40 opens $308.59, and a decisive break of $308.59 voids the trend thesis. Explicit gaps, not green lights: no sentiment report, a one-day news sample (20 of 175 records, all 07-28, nothing 07-22 to 07-27), no insider data, an unverified forward EPS estimate, no FY2025 baseline, and no valuation multiples beyond the derived P/E; the caller's holdings and cash are unknown, so sizing is a fraction of their own AAPL weight.

**Price Target**: 320.0

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, through the 2026-07-30 print and re-underwritten post-print

REFLECTION:
The five-day window (−8.0% raw, −13.6% alpha vs SPY) validated the reduce direction but punished the residual: trimming into $338–$345 dodged part of the decline, yet holding ~0.5x still surrendered double-digit alpha against a rising tape, and five days is too short to judge the full 1–3 month thesis into the 07-30 print. What it supports is the core evidence — the 38–42x multiple on unverified ~$8.40 EPS, the read that the year's deepest liquidity (261.8M on June 26) sat on the sell side, and the $320 target, which price essentially reached. What it undercuts is only sizing: the neutral one-third-to-one-half compromise, chosen to honor the intact trend stack, was the cost center, and the conservative two-thirds would have preserved materially more. The lesson for the next similar setup is that when a trim is anchored to a dated catalyst and an extreme multiple rather than momentum decay, the prior "trimming intact uptrends is expensive" priors should not shrink the cut — take the larger de-risk.

[2026-07-28 | AAPL | Underweight | -9.0% | -13.1% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AAPL at $340.08 — trim into strength, do not exit and do not add. Work a light 20–30% trim of the existing position with limit orders into the 338–343 pocket (priority near 342.89), taking exposure to roughly 70–75% of the firm's standard mega-cap weight; if already at or below ~70% of standard, do only a 5–10% token trim. No new capital, no averaging up, no leverage and no option overlays bought into the 28–29 July earnings/Fed window (no options-chain data was supplied). Hold the residual core against close-basis levels of 329.21, 319.35 and 307.83 (20% stub), and re-risk only after the event clears.

**Investment Thesis**: All three risk seats and the Research Manager converge on the same action — reduce exposure, keep a core — and the only live dispute is magnitude: aggressive 25–35% trim to 60–70% of standard, neutral 30–40% to 55–65%, conservative 35–45% to 50–60%. The direction is settled; the sizing is where the decision is made, and my own record argues for the light end.

Why reduce at all. The aggressive analyst actually supplied the deciding evidence against his own side: the plan's own entry math is ~2.0% to the 346.71 upper band against ~6.1% of structural risk to the 319.35 swing low (≈0.3:1), with the 10-EMA at 329.21 and 1× ATR at 332.00 both ~3.5% BELOW spot. The bull's "accumulate at 329–332 with a stop under 319.35" is a hold-the-core argument, not a buy argument, and his question to himself — "if the trend is this strong, why is your entry 3.5% lower?" — was never answered. On momentum quality, the MACD histogram is 1.310 versus a 3.337 peak while price sits at a record close, and RSI is 68.90 versus 71.65 on that same high — exactly the "RSI stalling below 71.65 on a price high" flip condition listed in the bull's own technical work. The breakout is thin: 5-day volume ~45.7M versus 20-day ~50.0M, price 4.2% above the VWMA at 326.48, and the report itself grades breakout quality "medium at best." On event asymmetry, the entire gross-margin thesis rests on ≥48.5%, yet the only print in the dataset is Q2 at 49.27%, there is no Q3 segment/mix data, no valuation multiple (P/E, EV/FCF, FCF yield) anywhere in the materials, and a Fed decision lands in the same 48-hour window — so "the business earned its multiple" is a claim the evidence cannot support. And the footnote risks the bull skipped land on the same line item the thesis depends on: an effective tax rate stepping 15.00% → 17.46% that persists in every forward quarter, buybacks −25.3% with capital returned down to 57% of FCF from ~107% and share count down only 0.71%, and a $12,777M intangible build with no matching cash acquisition outflow implying roughly $13B of future amortization aimed squarely at gross margin.

Why Underweight and not Sell. Nothing fundamental or structural has been falsified. H1 FY2026 revenue +16.1% to $254.9B (Q2 +16.6%), diluted EPS +19.8% to $4.85 (Q2 +21.8%), gross margin +169bp H1 and +222bp in Q2 to 49.27%, FCF +63.5% to $78.3B with CFO/NI at 1.15x, net cash nearly doubling to $61.9B. The tape is a clean fully ordered stack — 340.08 > 10-EMA 329.21 > VWMA 326.48 > 50-SMA 307.83 > 200-SMA 276.79 — with higher lows 245.51 → 245.70 → 273.75 → 319.35 and no confirmed RSI or MACD divergence. That is a core to keep, and the conservative analyst conceded as much ("I would not advocate a full exit"). Sell means exit or avoid entry; the plan is a partial de-risking, so Underweight is the correct label.

Why the light end, not the conservative's 35–45%. This is where prior lessons bind. The 2026-07-21, 2026-07-20, 2026-07-13, 2026-06-30 and 2026-07-01 AAPL Underweights each lost 3–8% of five-day alpha for the same reason: cutting inside a fully stacked rising structure on proximity to resistance or a single divergence, without a printed trigger. My 2026-07-20 reflection states the rule explicitly — require follow-through below the trigger before trimming, and keep any pre-print trim at the light end. Today that trigger is unfired: there is a momentum-quality divergence, but no close below 329.21, no lower low, no volume-confirmed distribution. The conservative ladder compounds the error — cutting another 20–25% of remaining exposure on a close below 329.21 is only ~3.3% below spot, ~1.35 ATR, the exact whipsaw mechanism the neutral flagged. I adopt the neutral's disciplined middle: light trim now for event-risk hygiene, a measured ladder (10–15% on the first rung, requiring volume/breadth confirmation) rather than an automatic one, 346.71 treated as an invalidation/review level rather than a protective stop since it sits above spot and shields nothing through a gap, and staged re-risking only after 29 July clears.

Data gaps stated rather than papered over: no valuation multiples of any kind, no Q3 FY2026 segment or product-mix data, no social sentiment, no options chain or IV to price a hedge, and a news sample of only 20 of 142 records all stamped 27 July with zero coverage of 21–26 July. Because the multiple is unmeasurable, sizing stays conservative. What would change the call: Q3 gross margin ≥48.5% with a credible intangible/amortization disclosure plus a volume-confirmed close above 342.89 upgrades to Overweight on a staged basis; a close below 307.83 on expanding volume, Q3 gross margin materially below 48.5%, confirmation that the 17.46% tax rate and cut buyback pace are structural, or adverse mix/receivables commentary converts this Underweight into a Sell.

**Price Target**: not provided

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, spanning the 28-29 July earnings/Fed window and the Q3 FY2026 print; re-underwritten post-event

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of -13.1% (raw -9.0% against a rising SPY) vindicates the Underweight direction outright, though the window spans only the 28–29 July event and cannot validate the 1–3 month re-underwriting plan. It supports the event-asymmetry leg of the thesis and undercuts the sizing argument: the light 20–30% trim captured only a fraction of what the conservative's 35–45% would have, and the 329.21 follow-through ladder fired only after the gap, so the discipline that was supposed to protect the position protected nothing through a binary catalyst. Lesson for next time: when the stated risk is a dated binary event, treat the event date itself as the trigger and size the pre-event trim at the heavier end rather than waiting for a close-basis confirmation that a gap will skip.

[2026-07-27 | AAPL | Hold | -9.9% | -12.5% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Hold

**Executive Summary**: Hold AAPL at benchmark weight (one standard allocation ≈ a 5% portfolio position). Put no new capital to work at the 2026-07-27 close of 336.91 and cap gross exposure at benchmark — trim only any excess above it, do not go below. Pre-commit one-third tranches that fire only after the 7/29–7/30 macro window and the FQ3 print clear: a pullback into 326–330 holding the 10 EMA (326.79) with VWMA 324.54 intact and RSI ≥45; a >339.57 daily close on ≥60M shares with the MACD histogram positive; or a clean post-earnings confirmation on margins, mid-teens revenue growth and an AI-monetization path — capped at one standard allocation total. **Investment Thesis**: The direction is settled and only the price is contested — and the tell is that all three risk seats independently refused to buy at the current print. Why not Sell/Underweight: the bull's substance was never dented — revenue +16.6%, gross margin 49.27% (+222bps YoY), operating income +21.3% ahead of revenue, H1 EPS +19.8%, ~$62B net cash, ~$78B FCF on capex −27.7%, with a fully stacked trend (price 21.9% above a rising 200 SMA at 276.38, 9.7% above a rising 50 SMA at 306.99, higher-low sequence 246.70 → 273.75 → 319.35 intact, VWMA rising to 324.54, no overhead supply above 339.57). Even the conservative analyst conceded it is a high-quality business and did not argue to reduce or short — capping how negative the call can honestly be. Why not Buy/Overweight at market: the bear won the arithmetic. From 336.91 upside to the 347.08 upper band is +3.0% versus −5.2% to the plan's 319.35 invalidation, −4.8% to the 320.63 stop and −8.9% to the 50 SMA — 1:1.6 to 1:3 against, with ATR 8.14 (2.42%) putting invalidation ~2.15 ATR away; the aggressive analyst's 2.5:1 applied only to the conditional 327 tranche, not the current tick. Three secondary bear points also stuck: unconfirmed breakout volume (47.5M/49.6M vs 60.96M/62.97M/63.41M on the prior leg; VWMA is backward-looking), two independent momentum divergences (MACD flat ~8.93 while price ran +3.2%; RSI 79.79 → 67.29 as price rose 8.0%), and the unexplained $12.8B gross / $13.3B → $25.8B net intangible jump — recast by the bull as 'option value' but ununderwritten until the filing shows an accretion path, especially with buybacks cut 25.3%. Add a ~35x back-of-envelope multiple (unverified, an annualization of H1 EPS) into a zero-disclosure print inside the Warsh press conference (7/29, 14:00 ET) and Thursday inflation data. Where the bear overreaches: the conservative analyst's demand to suspend Trigger B 'until the trend re-proves itself' is too rigid — the 60M-share/MACD-positive condition is itself a defined proof — and the sequential-margin comparison is a weaker test than the expanded YoY figure. The deciding synthesis is the neutral framework, which dominates both extremes: the aggressive analyst himself will not buy at 336.91 (his plan is scaled entries at 326–330 with a stop near 320.6, adding above 339.57 only on 60M+ volume) and the conservative analyst will not reduce. When the strongest advocate refuses to buy here and the strongest skeptic refuses to sell, the correct expression is Hold — maintain at benchmark, freeze new capital through the event, and let pre-committed triggers, not headlines, deploy the single standard allocation of incremental exposure afterward. Size for a ±2 ATR (~±5%) single-session move as normal, not a tail; if at or above benchmark and the desk can define event risk via puts/collar, hold the core rather than trading around the print. Upgrade to Overweight if the print shows YoY operating-margin expansion without soft AI commentary, EPS growth near the H1 ~20% pace, and a close above 339.57 on ≥60M shares. Downgrade to Underweight if a tranche is stopped at a close below 319.35, filing notes reveal a large all-time-high-priced acquisition with no accretion path while buybacks stay cut, or guidance points to sequential margin compression into FY2027. Gaps not closable from the material: no consensus, no guidance, no options-implied move, no short interest, no verified multiple, no filing confirmation of the intangible jump.

**Price Target**: 347.0

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months tactical, re-scored at the FQ3 print

REFLECTION:
The five-day window printed -9.9% raw and -12.5% alpha versus SPY, so the refusal to deploy new capital at 336.91 was correct in direction but the benchmark-weight Hold still absorbed nearly the whole drawdown; five days is too short to score a 1–3 month thesis, yet not too short to see that the ±2 ATR single-session sizing assumption badly understated a 5-day event-window move. What the window supports is the bear's asymmetry arithmetic (1:1.6 to 1:3 against buying) and the two momentum divergences plus unconfirmed breakout volume, which read as distribution rather than consolidation; what it undercuts is the bull's "fully stacked trend" and the 246.70 → 273.75 → 319.35 higher-low sequence, since a ~10% drop from 336.91 puts price through the 319.35 hard-review level and against the 306.99 50 SMA, meaning the plan's own trend-failure triggers should have fired. Lesson for the next similar setup: when the strongest advocate won't buy and the strongest skeptic won't sell, express that as reduced exposure rather than a frozen benchmark hold, and pre-commit a trim trigger alongside the additive tranches so a Hold cannot silently become a passive long into a 1:1.6–1:3 against payoff.
